copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Wednesday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Switzerland and Canada together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Canada side, by +15.5pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

On Elo, Canada comes in 30 points ahead — Switzerland at 1830, Canada at 1860. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Switzerland to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Canada to win at 39%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Switzerland to win at 45%, the draw at 27%, and Canada to win at 24%. The Canada side trades at 24% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +326. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 39%, +15.5pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Canada side that lower bound is 32% — +8.3pp clear of the market's 24%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 36 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Canada a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +15.5pp gap across model and market on the Canada side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Canada at 39%; Polymarket sits at 24%.
copy.title: Switzerland v Canada · the model leans Canada
